title: Copying a Word on the Simulated Tape
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Boolean Turing machine, let $y$ be a Boolean input word, and let $bits$ be a Boolean assignment to the selector-bit positions of $M$. For any Boolean word $rest$, natural number $p$, and Boolean words $w_X,w_C,w_O$, assume $1\le p$, $p+|rest|=|y|+1$, and the suffix of $y$ beginning at index $p-1$ is $rest$. Starting the machine that simulates $M$ in its copy state, with input head at the position obtained by clamping $p$ to the valid input-head range and buffers containing $w_X,w_C,w_O$, after $|rest|+1$ steps it is in the rewind-$X$ state at the right boundary, with the $X$ buffer containing $w_X$ followed by $rest$ and its head at position $|w_X\mathbin{+[0m[0m+}rest|-1$; the other buffers and their head positions are unchanged, and the output is empty.
caveat: The conclusion uses the explicitly defined simulator configurations and states; the informal descriptions supplied do not define those constructions fully.
